Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 80, verses 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called ʿAbasa (He frowned), because it opens with this human description, which is change of expression and frowning, as a rebuke to the Noble Prophet (ﷺ) for frowning in the face of ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum, the blind man.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• God teaches His Messenger (ﷺ) the more correct way of giving precedence among levels of benefit, through the story of ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum, when he came to the Messenger (ﷺ) asking him while he was calling some of the leaders of Quraysh. Within this is a reminder of honouring the believers, and an indication of the difference in situation between the polytheists who turn away from the guidance of Islam and the Muslims who come forward and follow it.

• An indication of the ingratitude of man despite the abundance of God's blessings upon him, and a mention of the signs of power in this universe, including God's facilitating for man the means of livelihood upon the surface of this earth.

• Evidence for the possibility of resurrection from the creation of man and the bringing forth of plants and trees from dead earth, a warning of the coming of the Hour, a mention of some of the terrors of the Resurrection, and a clarification of the state of believers and disbelievers on that Day.

[The Tafsir]

The change and frowning appeared on the face of the Messenger (ﷺ), and he turned away because the blind man ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum came to him seeking guidance, while the Messenger (ﷺ) was occupied with calling the leaders of Quraysh to Islam.

وأمّا من كان حريصًا على لقائك، وهو يخشى الله من التقصير في الاسترشاد، فأنت عنه تتشاغل. ليس الأمر كما فعلت -أيها الرسول-، إنَّ هذه السورة بما اشتملت عليه من الهداية موعظة لك ولكل من شاء الاتعاظ. فمن شاء ذكر الله وَأْتَمَّ بوحيه، هذا الوحي، وهو القرآن في صحف معظمة، موقرة، عالية القدر مطهرة من الدنس والزيادة والنقص، بأيدي ملائكة كتبة، سفراء بين الله وخلقه، كرام الخلق، أخلاقهم وأفعالهم بارة طاهرة.

Translation:

"As for one who came to you eager (for guidance), while he fears Allah (lest he fall short in seeking guidance), you were distracted from him. It is not as you did, O Messenger. Indeed, this surah, with the guidance it contains, is an admonition for you and for everyone who wishes to be admonished. So whoever wishes, let him remember Allah and follow His revelation, this revelation, which is the Qur'an, in honored, esteemed, high-ranking scrolls, purified from impurity, addition, and deficiency, in the hands of noble scribes, envoys between Allah and His creation, honorable in character, whose conduct and deeds are pious and pure."

This is a passage from the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 80, verses 8–16.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 80, verse 17–23:

﴿Cursed be the human being; how ungrateful he is!﴾ He is cursed and punished; how extremely disbelieving he is in his Lord! ﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾ Has he not considered from what thing Allah created him the first time? ﴿From a little water He created him and determined him in stages﴾ — that is, from a small quantity of water, which is the seminal fluid (al-manī). Then He determined him in stages (aṭwār), ﴿then He made the way easy for him﴾ — that is, He showed him the path of good and evil. ﴿Then He causes him to die and puts him in a grave﴾ — He made for him a place where he is buried. ﴿Then, when He wills, He will resurrect him﴾ — glorified is He; when He wills, He brings him back to life and raises him after his death for reckoning and recompense. ﴿Nay, but he has not fulfilled what He commanded him﴾ — the matter is not as the disbeliever says and does, for he has not carried out what Allah commanded him of faith and obedience through acts of worship.
